title: Sidecar multi-format log ingest with tenant-aware redaction and correlation-id normalization
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Add a small, language-agnostic sidecar process to application pods that normalizes multi-line and mixed-format logs into structured events suitable for high-throughput Loki ingestion while enforcing tenant-aware PII redaction and deterministic correlation-id canonicalization. Motivation: many services emit mixed JSON/plaintext/multiline stacks; current central ingest requires brittle per-service adapters. The sidecar will centralize parsing rules, provide CPU-local KV cache for short-lived identifiers, and emit a stable envelope (tenant_id, normalized_corr_id, timestamp_iso, schema_version, payload) to the cluster log router. Key features: (1) multiline boundary detection and incremental JSON streaming parsing (prefer simdjson/rapidjson bindings), (2) correlation-id normalization supporting traceparent, b3, x-request-id heuristics and fallback deterministic hashing, (3) tenant-aware redaction using configurable allowlist/denylist rules and regex patterns, with optional hash-preserving redaction for identifiers, (4) plug-in extraction hooks so services can opt-in structured fields, (5) batching and backpressure to keep per-pod CPU within limits and to push to Loki/ELK with configurable latency windows. Constraints: Must be lightweight (<=100MB resident, <5% CPU on medium pods), operate without changes to app logs where possible, and not change production log semantics unless explicitly enabled. Interops: output supports both Loki push API and an NDJSON stream for ELK ingestion. We will provide a conversion shim in the cluster router to map envelope fields to Loki labels for efficient queries (service, env, tenant, corr_id).
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar binary builds for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 and passes basic integration smoke tests
Multiline stacktraces (Java/Go/Python) correctly emitted as a single NDJSON event with original stack preserved under payload.stack and a normalized timestamp

Correlation id normalized: when traceparent present, extracted; when only x-request-id present, extracted; when none present, deterministic hashed id produced and stable for the lifetime of the process
Tenant redaction rules applied: PII patterns discovered in examples are redacted and hashed-preserved when configured
End-to-end ingestion into staging Loki shows <1% additional tail latency at P50 and P95 compared to current agent baseline and <5% CPU overhead on target service pod during test workload
Rollout playbook, rollback steps, and a runbook for incidents published and reviewed
Security review completed and signed off by security team
Automated tests covering parsing, redaction, corr-id heuristics, and backpressure behavior included in CI
tasks: Prototype parser with simdjson binding and a small finite-state multiline detector
Design redaction policy format and integrate with existing config service (feature-flag gated)
Implement corr-id normalizer: traceparent/b3/x-request-id + fallback hashing
Add Loki push adapter and NDJSON emitter for ELK compatibility
Create performance harness and benchmark against current fluentbit/agent baseline
Write unit+integration tests and add CI job
Prepare migration canary plan and rolling update strategy
Draft docs for SDKs/DevX describing opt-in hooks and observability labels
comments: 2026-02-20 Ava Patel: Initial discovery notes — scoped to sidecar approach after prototype showed easier ops surface than centralized adapters. Linked sample log corpus collected from staging.

2026-03-01 PM review (Lina Chen): Approved customer impact assessment; flagged enterprise tenants needing explicit allowlist for raw payload access. Suggested feature flag per-namespace for redaction strictness.
2026-03-04 Security note (Rakesh Singh): Security review requested — wants threat model for hash collisions and redact policy management. Assigned to security for formal signoff.

2026-03-07 DevOps (Marta Ivanova): Integration test with k8s DaemonSet vs sidecar per-pod trade-off discussed. Decided sidecar per-pod for tenant locality; follow-up to evaluate daemonset as lower-cost alternative for low-cardinality workloads.

2026-03-09 Diego Morales: Load test results attached — staging run with 200rps per pod showed 3% median CPU overhead and P95 ingestion latency +12ms vs baseline. Need to optimize JSON path extraction in hot code path.
